questions.question: One sentence: What does the Skill do?
questions.answer: NAS FlowPilot converts a project handoff request into a scoped, read-only NAS evidence review with a previewed plan and uncertainty-aware report.

questions.question: Who is the target user and problem?
questions.answer: Solo creators, small teams and project owners repeatedly need to verify required deliverables and conflicting file versions. Manual NAS browsing is slow and can falsely certify incomplete folders.

questions.question: What is your proposed solution?
questions.answer: An interactive NAS-native Skill asks for one approved project folder, exact deliverables and metadata permission, then coordinates only supported registered experts. Every reported finding is tied to evidence, with an explicit unknown state.

questions.question: What is the Core User Flow?
questions.answer: Owner requests a handoff check; the Skill clarifies folder and checklist, explains processing uncertainty, previews steps and seeks approval. The file expert lists authorized metadata; optional document review needs separate consent. The Skill returns PRESENT, MISSING, VERSION_REVIEW or NOT_CHECKED with next actions.

questions.question: What substantive difference does your idea offer compared with existing tools or conventional AI solutions?
questions.answer: Unlike a static checklist or generic chatbot, the plan adapts among handoff, missing-file, version-review and selected-document tasks, while disallowing scope expansion and fabricated complete scans. Owner-controlled NAS data remains the workflow's starting point.

questions.question: Which UGREEN AI NAS capabilities will be used, and at which step in the workflow?
questions.answer: The proposed registered file-agent uses catalog-listed ug-filesystem ls/find/stat for scoped discovery. An optional registered document-agent uses ug-document metadata/qa/extract/reconcile on consented exact references. Installed support and permissions require runtime verification.

questions.question: What was your technical approach? Describe the planned Skill workflow, supported NAS CLI capabilities, expert agent orchestration, required inputs, permissions, AI model choices, and data handling, as applicable;
questions.answer: A Markdown SKILL.md implements conversational input slots, plan preview, read-only expert delegation and evidence-based failure handling. Offline Python tests exercise parsing, permissions, version ambiguity and restricted paths but are not included in the ZIP. Data location is not assumed to be local; no arbitrary REST or external integrations are used.

questions.question: What is the current development status? Identify what was implemented already, not yet implemented, or is pending NAS validation if selected to be a Finalist.
questions.answer: A new FlowPilot Markdown candidate and separate offline planning/evidence modules exist. The candidate has not yet been generated or validated by the official Creator/checker. Actual registered-agent calls, real NAS operation, final permissions and publication approval are pending.

questions.question: What is your final validation plan? Name two core test cases and one edge case to validate if selected as a Finalist.
questions.answer: Core case one: a complete authorized delivery folder produces referenced file findings. Core case two: two plausible final versions cause VERSION_REVIEW, never automatic selection. Edge case: denied or truncated listing, restricted target or unverified symlink must produce NOT_CHECKED without data leakage.

questions.question: Are there any known limitations of your Project? Describe current known limitations, technical risks, and any external dependencies.
questions.answer: Official Creator compatibility, exact live dispatcher syntax, user permissions, data-processing location and real NAS completeness remain unverified. No scheduler, file mutation, generic n8n runtime or third-party SaaS connector is claimed. Final review requires explicit entrant approval.

disclosure: Entrant-directed concept and workflow; AI-assisted drafting and programming used OpenAI ChatGPT GPT-6. Earlier separate ProjectReady work used Codex; this new FlowPilot candidate has NOT been run through the official Uliya Creator. No UGREEN toolkit source or third-party executable is included in the proposed ZIP. UGREEN support described possible entrant license choices; no toolkit copyright or broader redistribution permission is claimed. Potential platform-hosted AI data processing is unverified. All actual NAS actions are proposed read-only, limited to the owner's explicit folder permission.
